title.zh: 镜像对称等离子体 Green 磁通矩阵

summary: Build a dense flux-response matrix for circular plasma-cell sources and targets sharing a reflection-symmetric rectilinear R-Z grid.

identity.relation: circular plasma-cell source currents to axisymmetric flux at the same R-Z grid points
identity.definition: Evaluate the maintained complete-elliptic-integral circular-filament flux response for sources on the first Z plane, then populate other source planes by the axial reflection and translation indexing permitted by the symmetric, uniformly spaced Z axis. Both matrix axes use C-order flattening of [Z,R]. No cell-area factor or current contraction is included.
identity.model: axisymmetric ideal circular-filament flux Green relation with source-compatible axial reflection construction
identity.geometry: source and target cells share a nonnegative-radius rectilinear R-Z mesh
identity.coordinates: SI cylindrical R-Z coordinates; grid arrays indexed [Z,R], matrix target and source axes flattened in C order
identity.boundary: A source radius within 1e-12 m of the axis yields a zero source column; nonfinite evaluated kernel elements, including unresolved singular values, are replaced by zero.
assumptions: The Z axis is strictly increasing, uniformly spaced and reflection-symmetric about zero within the implementation tolerances.
Each source column is a psi=R A_phi response per ampere of that circular source, not complete linked flux; the caller applies current or cell-current weights separately.

inputs.name: r_grid
inputs.description: Cylindrical radius mesh shared by source and target cells.
inputs.constraints: Finite, rectilinear, nonnegative and strictly increasing R axis; same shape as z_grid and at least two points per axis.

inputs.name: z_grid
inputs.description: Axial coordinate mesh shared by source and target cells.
inputs.constraints: Finite rectilinear grid with a strictly increasing, uniformly spaced and reflection-symmetric Z axis; same shape as r_grid and at least two points per axis.

outputs.name: g_psi
outputs.description: Psi=R A_phi response per source current for each target/source grid-cell pair.
outputs.constraints: Both axes follow C-order [Z,R] flattening; axis-source columns and nonfinite formula elements use the zero convention; no cell-area or 2*pi factor is included.

preconditions: Source and target are the same cylindrical R-Z mesh, with SI metre coordinates.
The axial grid is reflection-symmetric about zero and uniformly spaced at the declared numerical tolerances.
supported: Dense per-ampere flux Green matrices for the maintained ideal circular-source model on a symmetric R-Z grid.
excluded: Arbitrary nonuniform or nonsymmetric axial grids.
Independent target and source point sets or a non-axisymmetric geometry.
A resolved self-field, cell-area integration or automatic multiplication by source currents.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for wrong grid rank/shape, fewer than two points per axis, nonfinite coordinates, nonrectilinear grids, negative or non-increasing R axis, non-increasing Z axis, or Z symmetry/uniform-spacing violations.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: SciPy elliptic-function or unexpected NumPy errors propagate; nonfinite evaluated kernel elements are set to zero rather than raising.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative solver is used.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No matrix is returned when grid validation or execution raises; individual nonfinite kernel values follow the documented zero convention.

provenance.lineage_summary: Maintained SciRel relation mapped to a saved Pleiades L1 operator and direct tests. The historical admission mapping is development provenance only, not approval in the current SciRel lifecycle.
source_kinds: saved L1 operator document and implementation

example.description: Build a symmetric three-plane, four-radius response and check source-axis and axial-reflection blocks.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import build_mirror_plasma_flux_green
r_grid, z_grid = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(0.0, 0.3, 4), np.linspace(-0.4, 0.4, 3))
g_psi = build_mirror_plasma_flux_green(r_grid, z_grid)['g_psi']
assert g_psi.shape == (r_grid.size, r_grid.size)
assert np.isfinite(g_psi).all()
for source_plane in range(3):
    np.testing.assert_allclose(g_psi[:, source_plane*4], 0.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(g_psi[0:4, 4:8], g_psi[4:8, 0:4])
example.expected: A finite 12-by-12 float64 flux-response matrix with zero axis-source columns and equal blocks for equal axial plane separation.

scope: First source-plane columns against an independently written circular-filament formula.
Whole-matrix equality with direct dense filament columns on a symmetric grid.
Square shape, finite output and axis-source zero-column convention.
Rejection of an axially nonsymmetric grid and reflection-block relation.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct SciRel tests establish selected source-plane formula values, indexing invariants and one invalid-grid case. They do not prove resolved self-fields, arbitrary-grid validity, whole-project reassembly or expert recognition of this development record.
known_limitations: The result is a dense O((N_Z*N_R)^2) matrix and may be costly on large grids.
Near-axis source columns and nonfinite kernel values use a zero convention rather than a physical singularity model.
Current contraction and cell-area factors are caller responsibilities.
Public distribution licensing and SciRel expert recognition remain pending.
